title: Strong Quantum Mpemba Effect from Exact Slow-Mode Selection in Constrained Rydberg Chains
authors: Mingdi Xu, Kaixiang Lu, Xiang-Ping Jiang, Haiping Hu, Lei Pan
abstract: Can a many-body state relax faster because it is blind to the slowest decay channel? We show that this mechanism gives rise to a robust strong quantum Mpemba effect in locally dephased constrained Rydberg chains. The key observation is that, for constrained single-spin-flip Hamiltonians, local dephasing turns the Hamiltonian itself into an exact left Liouvillian slow mode,   $\mathcal L^\dagger(H)=-γH$.   A thermal state generically retains this slow channel, whereas translationally invariant states with vanishing energy expectation remove it and are forced to relax through faster visible modes. This exact selection rule produces a strong quantum Mpemba effect in the locally dephased PXP chain, including for a zero-energy scar eigenstate, the $|0\cdots0\rangle$ product state, and a translation-invariant $Z_2$ cat state. We further show that the same mechanism persists in the $(2,3)$ model and in the longer-range blockade family. Our results identify exact slow-mode selection, rather than special scar wave functions, as a general organizing principle for anomalously fast relaxation in constrained open quantum systems.
summary: The paper reveals that an anomalously fast relaxation, or strong quantum Mpemba effect, can occur in constrained Rydberg chains due to a mechanism of exact slow-mode selection. This selection rule forces the system's evolution away from the slowest thermal decay channel into faster visible modes. The finding establishes this spectral criterion as a general principle for understanding accelerated non-equilibrium dynamics.
main_problem: Investigating anomalous fast relaxation phenomena, specifically a 'strong quantum Mpemba effect,' where an initially farther state relaxes faster than a closer one in non-equilibrium dynamics.
main_result: The strong quantum Mpemba effect is shown to arise from the exact selection of slow Liouvillian modes when specific constraints (energy and symmetry) are met, rather than relying on special wave functions.
method: Theoretical analysis involving the structure of the left Liouvillian ($\mathcal L^\dagger(H)=- \gamma H$) and analyzing decay rates using the trace distance in time evolution.
model_or_system: The study focuses on locally dephased constrained Rydberg chains, exemplified by the PXP model and its generalizations like the (2, 3) model. The dynamics are governed by single-spin-flip Hamiltonians under local dephasing.
key_observables: The rate of decay measured by the trace distance ($	ext{D}_{	ext{tr}}$); the ratio $\eta$ comparing fast vs. thermal relaxation rates.
important_parameters: Local dephasing strength ($\gamma$); system size (Hilbert-space dimension $D$).
main_assumptions: The mechanism relies on the specific structure of single-spin-flip Hamiltonians under local dephasing, and the selection rule is shown to be general.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate that selected initial states relax asymptotically faster than the thermal reference state in the PXP chain across different constrained models.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (SQME), derives the necessary two-part selection rule based on Liouvillian structure, and then demonstrates this rule's applicability to various constrained Rydberg chain models.
why_interesting: This work provides a general organizing principle—exact slow-mode selection—for understanding anomalous fast relaxation in open quantum systems, linking spectral properties (Liouvillians) directly to macroscopic non-equilibrium dynamics like the Mpemba effect.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Strong quantum Mpemba effect in the locally dephased PXP chain. Periodic boundary conditions, L = 18, D = 5778, γ = 0.4, and β = 0.25 are used. (a) Spectral weight Wn used to identify the representative zero-energy scar eigenstate. (b) Energy-basis diagonal weights of ρss and ρth. (c) Control states violating one of the two selection conditions in Eq. (2). (d–f) Three selected states satisfying Eq. (2) relax faster asymptotically than the same thermal reference.

FIG. 2. Cross-model SQME from the same selection rule. Each panel compares a translation-invariant cat state with Tr(Hρ0) = 0 to the thermal reference ρth. Periodic boundary conditions, γ = 0.1, β = 0.25, and γt ≤10 are used. The models are (a) the (2, 3) model, L = 12, D = 1499; (b) PPXPP, L = 21, D = 3063; (c) PPPXPPP, L = 24, D = 2287; and (d) PPPPXPPPP, L = 30, D = 4612.

Figure 4 provides a direct mode-resolved check in the standard PXP chain. Some of the globally slow nonsteady modes lie in nonzero-Q sectors and are therefore invisible to translationally invariant density matrices. Within the visible Q = 0 sector, the exact H-like mode is the slowest thermal channel, while the next non-H mode decays faster. This explains why the thermal state has a slower tail, whereas states satisfying Eq. (2) bypass this tail and relax through the faster Q = 0 channel. The spectral structure in Fig. 4 is therefore the mode-space counterpart of the time-domain crossings shown in Figs. 1 and 2.

FIG. 3. Visible-rate ratio η = rfast/rth versus constrained Hilbert-space dimension D. The (2, 3) model is not an R- blockade member. All data use periodic boundary conditions, local dephasing, γ = 0.1, and β = 0.25. Values above unity indicate asymptotically faster relaxation than the thermal reference; the accessible-size trend shows no rapid collapse of the selected-state advantage.

FIG. 4. Operator momenta of slow Liouvillian modes in the locally dephased PXP chain with L = 18 and γ = 0.4. Translationally invariant density matrices couple only to Q = 0 modes. The H-like mode has rate rH = γ, while the next visible non-H mode in the Q = 0 sector has a larger decay rate. Imposing Tr(Hρ0) = 0 removes the H-like mode and leaves the faster visible channel.
